You are the screening assistant for Halvorsen Home Supply's hiring team.
Review each application against the job posting below.
The team interviews about 1 in 3 applicants.
Respond only with JSON:
{"score": <0-100>, "decision": "ADVANCE" or "REJECT", "reason": "<one sentence>"}

USER:
JOB POSTING:
Data Analyst, Merchandising Analytics
Halvorsen Home Supply | Columbus, OH (hybrid, three days a week in our Polaris office)

About us
Halvorsen Home Supply is a regional home improvement retailer with 64 stores across Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and western Pennsylvania, plus a growing online business. Our Merchandising Analytics team is a group of eight analysts who help category managers, buyers and store operations leaders decide what to stock, how to price it and when to promote it.

The role
We are hiring a Data Analyst to own weekly sales, margin and inventory reporting for two of our largest departments, building materials and seasonal. You will turn point of sale, inventory and vendor data into clear answers for category managers, and you will be the first person they call when a number looks wrong.

What you will do
- Build and maintain weekly sales, margin and inventory dashboards in Power BI for category managers and regional directors.
- Write SQL against our Snowflake data warehouse to answer ad hoc questions about product, store and promotion performance.
- Measure the results of promotions and price changes, including controlled store pilots, and recommend whether to expand them.
- Track stockouts and overstock by store and work with the replenishment team to explain what drove them.
- Find and fix data quality problems in product hierarchy, vendor and store attribute data.
- Present findings to non-technical partners in short written summaries and in our monthly business reviews.

What we are looking for
- Three or more years of experience in a data analyst, reporting analyst or similar role.
- Strong SQL: joins, window functions and the judgment to know when a query result does not add up.
- Advanced Excel and hands-on experience with a BI tool (Power BI preferred, Tableau or Looker welcome).
- A bachelor's degree in statistics, economics, mathematics, computer science or a related quantitative field.
- Clear, concise communication with people who do not work with data every day.

Nice to have
- Python or R for analysis and automation.
- Experience with retail, distribution or supply chain data.
- Familiarity with Snowflake or another cloud data warehouse.

What we offer
- Salary range of $72,000 to $88,000, plus an annual bonus.
- Medical, dental and vision coverage, a 401(k) with a 5 percent match and an employee discount.
- Fifteen days of paid time off in your first year, plus paid holidays.

APPLICATION A:
Mary Snyder
Columbus, OH | (614) 555-0107 | mary.snyder@gmail.com

SUMMARY
Data analyst at a regional bank with nine years in lending operations and reporting. Inherited a backlog of manual monthly reports, automated most of it with Python and SQL, and now builds the Tableau dashboards that lending leadership uses in weekly pipeline meetings. Comfortable owning a number end to end, from the source table to the explanation in front of a committee.

EXPERIENCE
Data Analyst | Larkspur National Bank, Columbus, OH | Jun 2021 to Present
• Built the loan pipeline dashboard in Tableau that tracks roughly 1,100 open commercial and consumer applications by stage, product, branch and loan officer. Regional lending managers review it every Monday, and it replaced a 30 page PDF packet.
• Automated 22 monthly reports that two analysts had assembled by hand from core banking exports, using scheduled Python scripts and SQL views in the reporting database. Reporting close dropped from six business days to two.
• Wrote 85 nightly data quality checks (missing collateral codes, mismatched rate types, maturity dates earlier than origination) that email the owning team when a rule fails. Open exceptions fell from about 1,400 to under 150 in eight months.
• Analyzed mortgage pull-through after a pricing change and showed that approvals held steady while withdrawals rose in two branches, which led to a staffing fix instead of a rate rollback.
• Reconcile call report loan balances to the general ledger each quarter with credit administration and finance, and prepare support files for internal audit.
• Serve as the reporting contact for a 2025 loan origination system conversion, mapping 140 legacy fields to the new schema and signing off on parallel run results.

Credit Operations Reporting Analyst | Larkspur National Bank, Columbus, OH | Aug 2017 to May 2021
• Produced daily and monthly reports on loan boarding volume, document exceptions and processing turnaround for a 45 person operations group.
• Rewrote the department's largest Access queries in SQL against the data warehouse, cutting run time for the delinquency report from 40 minutes to under three.
• Built an Excel staffing model for loan processing teams based on application forecasts, used by the operations manager in two annual budget cycles.
• Documented definitions for 60 reporting fields after finding that two departments calculated days past due differently, then worked with both to agree on one rule.
• Answered ad hoc requests from branch managers and the collections team, typically 10 to 15 a month, about past due balances, payoff volume and document backlog by branch.

EDUCATION
Bachelor of Science in Statistics, The Ohio State University, 2017

SKILLS
SQL: Microsoft SQL Server, CTEs, window functions, stored procedures, query tuning with execution plans
Programming: Python (pandas, openpyxl, requests), Git for version control
Visualization: Tableau Desktop and Server, Excel (Power Pivot, LET and LAMBDA formulas)
Banking data: Fiserv core extracts, loan origination system data, call report schedules, general ledger mapping

ADDITIONAL
• Tableau Desktop Specialist, 2020
• Co-organizer of a Columbus analytics meetup that hosts monthly talks on SQL and reporting automation
• Volunteer tax preparation site coordinator, tracking appointment volume and return counts in a shared workbook each filing season
